text: At the left side of the pitch near the Harbour City goal, Elias Okafor scores the opening goal for Harbour City just before halftime after a patient buildup involving 17 passes and a through ball from Marek Barros at 45 minutes [#904] [#905]. Right after the break, Barros finds space at around 44 metres from the Seabrook goal on the right and scores with a long cross from a corner, giving Harbour City a 2-0 lead despite being down to 10 players following a red card at 43 minutes [#870] [#975]. Seabrook Town responds from the central right side around 10 metres out at 53 minutes with Tariq Marlowe’s goal. Later, Callum Varga scores at 69 minutes assisted from the right flank after a quick passing sequence [#1448]. In stoppage time at the Harbour City end, Kian Romano scores twice within minutes: first on a counterattack from the central area 7 metres out at 90+2 and then from close range on the left flank assisted by Tomas Kowalski, completing Seabrook’s comeback to win 4-2 [#1882] [#1906]. Seabrook’s wide, crossing attack finally shifts to high pressing and direct play after 65 minutes, overwhelming Harbour City despite their initial control [#1361].

social: Seabrook Town scores two stunning stoppage-time goals to win 4-2 away at Harbour City!
Marek Barros shines with a goal and two assists but Seabrook Town’s second half fightback seals the comeback.
Red card toughens Harbour City, but Seabrook Town's pressing and wide play turn the game around.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for audio audience in en

- Seabrook Town dominated the second half with 4 goals and 2.71 xG, overturning a 2-1 deficit to win 4-2 [#1448, #1882].
- Marek Barros (Harbour City) scored a goal with only 0.009 xG and provided 2 assists with 5 key passes and 9 interceptions [#975].
- Kian Romano scored twice late goals in stoppage time (90+2' and 90+3') with high xG of 0.609 and 0.959 to complete the comeback [#1882, #1906].
- Harbour City suffered a red card to Joon Whitfield at 43', reducing them to 10 men before their two quick goals around half-time [#870, #871].
- Seabrook Town had better overall stats: 22 shots vs 10, 53.4% possession, 3 big chances vs 1, and 9 corners vs 6 [team_stats].

- Seabrook Town scored their third goal at 90+2' through Kian Romano in a counter-attack after a ball regain by Romano himself; a quick two-pass sequence with Aiden Quinlan created the chance, reflecting their aggressive, wide, crossing style turning into direct counterattacks late in the game [#1881,#1882].
- The equalizing goal reflects a higher pressing and more direct play change by Seabrook from minute 65 onwards—their line height and pressing increased, indicating a tactical shift to chase the game after trailing 2-1. This alteration boosted their ability to regain possession higher and launch faster attacks [#1361].
- Harbour City relied on patient short passing build-ups, as demonstrated by their first goal at 45’ with a long sequence of 17 passes over 57 seconds involving multiple players before Marek Barros assisted Okafor through a through ball. This methodical play fits their 4-2-3-1 formation and style of play [#904,#905].
- Marek Barros, playing a pivotal playmaker role, scored from a rare long cross at 47' after a corner initiation, showing despite their emphasis on short passing, set pieces and individual creativity were also important in Harbour City's offensive patterns [#973,#975].
- Seabrook Town’s formation of 3-4-3 supports their wide, crossing play style and allows them to press higher with more wing presence, supported by increased possession and box touches compared to Harbour City, who showed fewer box touches and less possession, reflecting their more cautious buildup [overall stats].
